construct: UGT1A1 in hepatocytes conjugates bilirubin with glucuronic acid, rendering it water soluble for biliary excretion. Near-complete or complete loss of UGT1A1 activity in Crigler-Najjar type I causes severe persistent unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia and risk of bilirubin encephalopathy; phenobarbital is ineffective because there is essentially no residual enzyme activity to induce.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Severe neonatal isolated unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia without hemolysis or hepatocellular injury and no phenobarbital response indicates Crigler-Najjar type I from absent UGT1A1 activity.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Bilirubin-production enzymes are upstream and MRP2 transports already-conjugated bilirubin; neither explains isolated severe unconjugated bilirubin with absent inducibility.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The bilirubin fraction, normal hemolysis workup, and lack of phenobarbital response identify defective UGT1A1 glucuronidation as the only direct answer.
